data.name: PTEN
data.description: Phosphatase that erases PIP3 and so shuts down the PI3K arm. One of the most frequently lost tumour suppressors in human cancer, and one of the most common ways this pathway is left switched on without its growth-factor brake.
data.description_beginner: A tumor-suppressing enzyme that erases the 'go' signal generated by PI3K, shutting that branch of the pathway down. It's one of the genes most frequently lost in human cancer, and losing it is one of the most common ways this pathway is left switched on without its growth-factor brake.

reading_levels.student: Lipid phosphatase that converts PIP3 back to PIP2.
reading_levels.research: PTEN does not inhibit the PI3K enzyme; it dephosphorylates PI3K's product, PIP3. Haploinsufficient tumour suppressor with dose-dependent phenotypes.

studies.title: PTEN regulates microtubule polymerization via mTORC2, but not mTORC1, in peripheral sensory neurons
studies.authors: Evans S; Reglewski J; Rose H; Lewis C; Nayak A; Minsky C; McNeil E; Knowles B; Wang W; Li M; Luikart BW; Hong J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse peripheral sensory neuron cultures (Pten-KO with Raptor or Rictor co-deletion, both sexes)
studies.finding: Uses Raptor (mTORC1) versus Rictor (mTORC2) co-deletion on a Pten-knockout background to ask which complex carries the growth signal to the microtubule cytoskeleton. Suppressing mTORC2 — but not mTORC1 — returns the accelerated microtubule polymerisation and neuronal hypertrophy of Pten-KO neurons to wild-type levels, and the effect is confined to the axonal growth cone rather than the proximal axon shaft. A clean genetic dissection on the comparatively thin mTORC2 side of the pathway.

studies.title: Identification of the tuberous sclerosis complex-2 tumor suppressor gene product tuberin as a target of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/akt pathway
studies.authors: Manning BD; Tee AR; Logsdon MN; Blenis J; Cantley LC

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mammalian cell lines (mouse 3T3 cells, human cells) and PTEN-null tumour-derived cell lines; in vitro kinase assays
studies.finding: The authors combined biochemistry with a search for Akt consensus motifs and picked out tuberin, the TSC2 tumour suppressor protein, as a likely Akt substrate. They showed that activating PI3K leads to phosphorylation of tuberin at sites matching the Akt motif, and that Akt can phosphorylate tuberin both in vitro and in cells. Two of these sites, S939 and T1462, were regulated by PI3K, and T1462 stayed phosphorylated in tumour cell lines lacking PTEN. A tuberin mutant without the main PI3K-dependent sites blocked activation of S6K1. Together with papers from other labs in the same months, this was one of the early papers to link growth-factor signalling through Akt to the TSC complex and mTORC1 output. Boundary: cultured mammalian cells and in vitro kinase assays, with overexpressed tuberin mutants; no whole-animal or human tissue data.

studies.title: Enhanced sensitivity of PTEN-deficient tumors to inhibition of FRAP/mTOR
studies.authors: Neshat MS; Mellinghoff IK; Tran C; Stiles B; Thomas G; Petersen R; Frost P; Gibbons JJ; Wu H; Sawyers CL

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Isogenic PTEN+/+ and PTEN-/- mouse cells and human cancer cell lines, in vitro and as tumours in mice; CCI-779
studies.finding: Tested whether tumour cells that have lost PTEN depend more on mTOR. The rapamycin analogue CCI-779 (temsirolimus) blocked growth of PTEN-null cells and tumours preferentially, and reversed the extra tumour growth caused by constitutively active Akt, placing mTOR downstream of Akt in tumour formation. PTEN loss went with higher S6 kinase activity and S6 phosphorylation. Sensitivity was not explained by how well the drug blocked S6 phosphorylation, since S6 was inhibited in sensitive and resistant lines alike. Boundary: worked from the abstract only (scanned PMC record); mouse and human cell lines and mouse tumour models, not patients.

studies.title: An inhibitor of mTOR reduces neoplasia and normalizes p70/S6 kinase activity in Pten+/- mice
studies.authors: Podsypanina K; Lee RT; Politis C; Hennessy I; Crane A; Puc J; Neshat M; Wang H; Yang L; Gibbons J; Frost P; Dreisbach V; Blenis J; Gaciong Z; Fisher P; Sawyers CL; Hedrick-Ellenson L; Parsons R

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Pten+/- mice treated with a pharmacological mTOR inhibitor
studies.finding: Transformed cells in Pten+/- mice showed raised phosphorylated Akt and active p70 S6 kinase together with faster proliferation. Treating the mice with an mTOR inhibitor reduced neoplastic proliferation, tumour size and S6 kinase activity without changing Akt status. The authors concluded that S6K and possibly other mTOR targets contribute to tumour development downstream of PTEN loss. Boundary: worked from the abstract only (scanned PMC record); mouse model. The abstract does not name the inhibitor.

relations.mechanism: PTEN erases PIP3, undoing PI3K. Losing PTEN is one of the commonest ways a tumour leaves this whole axis switched on without an upstream signal.
relations.mechanism_beginner: PTEN erases the lipid signal that PI3K makes. Losing PTEN is one of the most common ways cancers keep this whole pathway switched on without any signal from outside.
relations.context: The 'inhibits' label describes the net effect on signalling, not the enzyme itself: PTEN does not inhibit PI3K catalytically, and Maehama & Dixon reported PI3K activation itself unchanged. PTEN dephosphorylates PIP3, PI3K's lipid product, erasing the signal downstream of the enzyme rather than blocking the enzyme's activity.
relations.boundary: The arrow is drawn PTEN -> PI3K for readability, but PTEN does not act on the PI3K enzyme. It dephosphorylates PIP3, PI3K's lipid product, so the effect on PI3K signalling is indirect and the edge is a compressed one whose hidden intermediate is PIP3. The canonical biochemical demonstration (Maehama & Dixon, J Biol Chem 1998, PMID 9593664) sits outside this corpus: purified recombinant PTEN dephosphorylates PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 specifically at position 3, and in the same paper PTEN overexpression reduced insulin-induced PIP3 without affecting insulin-induced PI3K activation. The cancer-genetics support in-corpus is mouse (GUE2009).
relations.note: 2026-10-09: Causal directness changed direct -> indirect to match the prose. PTEN removes PI3K's product (PIP3) rather than acting on PI3K itself, so 'direct' was inconsistent with the mechanism and context text. Interaction type stays 'dephosphorylation' (what PTEN does to PIP3). 2026-10-10: Interaction type changed dephosphorylation -> functional-consequence. Leaving a reaction type on an edge whose target is the PI3K protein made the machine-readable claim 'PTEN dephosphorylates PI3K', which the prose had always contradicted. The edge is now typed as what it is, a compressed functional opposition, with PIP3 named as the hidden intermediate.
